:::{#exm-accumulation-function}
#### The accumulation function of a constant

Let $f(t) = 2$ on $[0, 3]$, which is Riemann integrable (@exm-integrable-constant).
For $0 < x \le 3$, the computation of @exm-integrable-constant,
with the interval $[0, 3]$ replaced by $[0, x]$, gives

$$
\ba
F(x)
&= \int_0^x 2\,dt
&& \text{(definition of the accumulation function)}
\\
&= 2 \cd (x - 0)
&& \text{(every Riemann sum is } 2 \text{ times the total width } x - 0 \text{)}
\\
&= 2x
&& \text{(subtract)}
\ea
$$

and $F(0) = 0 = 2 \cd 0$ too.
For example, $F(1.5) = 2 \cd 1.5 = 3$, the area of a rectangle of height $2$ and width $1.5$.

:::
